plain: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that Garry Nolan, a Stanford scientist who studies the immune system, has been looking into the brains of people who report UFOs, and has working theories that are not final. As Michels tells it, Nolan says people with more densely packed brain cells in the caudate and putamen, two parts of a deep brain region called the basal ganglia, are more likely both to see UFOs and to be, in Michels's words, more psychic. Michels adds that this trait runs in families, which would give some people a built-in reason for seeing what others don't.
